Point blank, every pellet landing. One column per health pool rather than per hero, because every 225 health hero dies to the same count. This is the number that settles a duel: not damage per second, but whether they die to two shots or three.
A non-commercial fan project. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Blizzard Entertainment.

Hero, ability and perk names come from Blizzard, who publish the game in ten of the fifteen languages this app speaks. In the rest they stay in English, and nothing on this end can change that: the words have to come from somebody who plays the game in that language.

Still in English: Simplified Chinese, Ukrainian, Swedish, Arabic, Turkish. Also the Stadium armoury, in every language, because Blizzard do not publish those names at all. Partial help is welcome — a name with no translation falls back to English, so nobody has to finish a language to be useful.
One file on GitHub, and how to add to it
Hero statistics, abilities, release dates and the full balance history come from the Overwatch Wiki, licensed CC BY-SA.
Portraits, ability icons and the hero roster come from Blizzard\'s own site through the OverFast API.
The damage simulation and its 2020 reference dataset derive from owdmgchart by yfp, MIT licensed.
Hero portraits, ability icons, names and artwork are the property of Blizzard Entertainment, used under Blizzard\'s Fan Content Policy. This app is free, carries no advertising and sells nothing.

Ranked by the damage one cast can deal. An ultimate is burst, not sustained fire, so this is not a damage-per-second figure.
Healing per second, reload included. An ally being healed is not dodging, so this is arithmetic rather than simulated.
Pick a hero to see their details.
No saved builds for this hero yet.
Buffs apply to weapons only: an ultimate deals what it deals, and damage boost is not what multiplies healing.

Stats are exact for every item. The damage figure is a full simulation, but only Weapon Power and Attack Speed feed into it - the model cannot compute what ability power or cooldowns are worth, so a build that leans on those will be undersold here.

This is the one screen that needs a connection. The rest of the app works offline because a weapon\'s numbers and a patch that already happened do not change; which heroes are being banned changes every week, so it is fetched rather than shipped.

Figures published by Blizzard on overwatch.blizzard.com, one row per hero and broken down by region only. Their page offers filters for map, rank and queue; every one of them returns the same numbers, so this app no longer shows controls that would change nothing. It also means no win rate per map, and no win rate per team composition — Blizzard publish neither, and multiplying single-hero rates together would invent a figure rather than find one. Nothing here is stored on your phone.

Written by the wiki from the perspective of playing this hero. Where an editor graded the matchup, their wording is shown as-is; rows without a grade were never graded, and no verdict has been inferred for them. Tap a portrait to open that hero.
Do not mention this version again
Version %1$s is out, and this one has to be installed by hand

This version is signed with a new key, so Android will not install it over the copy you have: it would just say the app was not installed, without saying why.

Download the new file first, then uninstall this one, then install what you downloaded. Uninstalling before the download leaves you with no app and nowhere to get it from.

Saved boards and settings do not survive the uninstall, so export any plan you want to keep as a PDF first.

It is a one-off. Updates after this one install normally again.

Your career, looked up by BattleTag. There is no sign-in because there is nothing to sign in to: Blizzard publish no Overwatch API, so the only source is the career profile they publish for players who have set theirs to public. Type the whole tag — Name#1234 — to go straight to one.

Not found. Try the whole BattleTag with its number, like Name#1234, which addresses a profile directly. If that fails too, the profile is almost certainly private: Blizzard only publishes — and only lets anything search — profiles set to public in the game, under Options, Social, Career Profile.
This profile exists, but its career statistics are not public. That is a setting inside Overwatch — Options, Social, Career Profile — and nothing this app can do from the outside.
Career profiles come from Blizzard through the OverFast API. Only the BattleTag you pick is stored, and only on this phone.

BYZ, MrStoneStar, MizuBluee and Nana played with this and reported what was wrong: Bastion stuck in Recon, Ashe reloading twelve rounds in half a second, the turrets that were missing, the meta role filter that changed nothing, and a good deal more. Several numbers in this app are right because they said so.
%1$s tokens of Claude Code, up to version %2$s.

Every ability once, then a melee, then the hardest-hitting weapon — one shot, or one second for a beam — all at point-blank. Computed from the same figures the rest of the app uses, because the wiki describes combos only in prose. It assumes everything lands on one target and each thing is used once: an orb that bounces back for a second pass is worth more than this says — that is a real figure, just one that depends on the bounce rather than on the hero.
Total, over about %1$.1f s of casting
The whole opening each hero has on one target: every ability once, a melee, then the hardest single shot — one second for a beam. Best case, assuming everything lands and nothing repeats.
Tap a hero to place them. Drag a token to move it, long press to remove.
World is the mean of Europe, Americas and Asia, weighted equally. Blizzard publish no worldwide figure and no player counts to weight by.

Relative Aim Sensitivity While Zoomed is a percentage of your hip sensitivity, set per hero. A full turn takes the same distance of mouse at 100%; lower values match how the scope looks rather than how far it turns.
Movement at the middle of the screen matches, following the perspective properly. Known as 0% monitor distance.
The plain ratio of the two fields of view. Cruder, because a screen is flat, but it holds up better towards the edges.

Type the setting that already feels right on %1$s, and the field of view of the scope you want to match. The slider above does not affect this: two scopes compared against the same hip view are compared against each other.
same feel, on the scope you entered

Only Ana and Widowmaker have had their scopes measured, and both zoom to 50.94. Blizzard publish no figure for the others, and the numbers passed around for them are estimates, so type one in rather than be given a guess.

Stars and a written review go to the Play listing, where Google keeps them. Anything wrong with a number belongs in the issue tracker instead, where it can be answered and fixed.
This copy was installed by hand, so there is no store listing to rate on. Anything wrong with a number belongs in the issue tracker, where it can be answered and fixed.
Blizzard\'s own photograph of each map. A top-down diagram is better to plan on, but those belong to whoever drew them, so bring your own if you have one.
Guides by people who play them. The app does not write these: every number here is traceable, and how to play at a given rank is judgement rather than data.
Shots to kill, at point blank. A whole number that does not move with how well you aim - which is what decides a duel.
Numbers in this app get fixed because people who play the game say when they are wrong. One report is marked as correct-as-it-stood rather than fixed, with the reasoning in the repository.

Can this kill that. Two answers, because the honest one has two halves: how many shots it takes with nothing healing, which decides almost every real fight, and whether the damage out-paces the healing, which decides the ones that last.
Nothing gives. The damage and the healing cancel out.
It does not die. Firing longer will not change that.
%1$d shots, if every one lands and nothing heals.
%1$d shots, or %2$d to the head, if every one lands and nothing heals.

Perks appear as separate rows, named after the perk. Only the ones that change a weapon\'s numbers whatever happens are drawn: a range, a projectile speed, an ammo cost. The ones that depend on the fight going a certain way, like landing two scoped shots in a row or catching an enemy below half health, are left out rather than guessed at.
This app is built by one person, who plays Overwatch 2 and streams it. In some of these rooms you will find me; the rest are public places that have been around for years.
